newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares firm as job cuts help Leykam.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares firm as job cuts help Leykam.

text.p: Austrian shares closed higher on Thursday after a volatile trading session, helped by strong demand for paper maker Leykam after the group late on Wednesday said it planned to cut 500 jobs at its Austrian plant.

The ATX index of 21 blue chips rose 6.56 points or 0.56 percent to close at 1,186.86, below the day's high of 1,192.45. Among its constituents, 13 gainers outnumbered five losers, three shares were unchanged.

Traders said the index was likely to breach 1,200 points in the next few days, but expected the market to take a short breather before resuming its advance. The ATX has risen 4.1 percent since the start of the year.
"The direction is looking pretty good," said a trader.
Leykam, a subsidiary of Dutch KNP BT, surged 8.14 percent to close at 293, following a last-minute bout of profit taking after the shares hit an intraday high of 296.
Steel maker Boehler-Uddeholm rose 14 to 790 schillings, while VA Stahl was up 1.4 schillings at 417 despite the report of a 48 percent slump in 1996 net earnings on Tuesday.
Brick maker Wienerberger closed steady at 2,190 before the group announced a 13 percent drop in 1996 pre-tax earnings.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index rose 1.62 points or 0.37 percent to finish at 441.83.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, ATX contracts for February delivery were up seven points at 1,192.0.
